claims.statement: The query-service is SANDMAN's only user entry point: the /v1 REST API authenticates with bearer tokens only and the server-rendered console under /console uses a session cookie, while owner services (extraction-agent, inconsistency-agent, orchestrator) are never user-facing; the service authenticates the caller, checks the operation's minimum role loaded from the OpenAPI contract, and forwards operations to owners.

Service.authenticate resolves a bearer token to a Principal in two stages: first via the shared service-token hash map (a hit is a service, or a plugin when the caller name has the plugin: prefix, with grants from config/query/plugins.yaml), then as a personal API token in the user store; a user with must_change_password set gets 403 even with a valid token.
/v1/* never accepts the session cookie: POST /v1/auth/login sets it, POST /v1/auth/logout revokes it, and every other API route authenticates from the Authorization header only.
Login is rate-limited in memory: 5 failures per username or per client address within 15 minutes produce HTTP 429 with Retry-After 900.

Restricted personal tokens (project-scoped or role-capped) cannot create or revoke tokens: both /v1/auth/tokens POST and DELETE return 403 for them, and an unrestricted admin requires no token projectId and no maxRole.

Object-addressed operations without a projectId in the path (getInconsistency, transitionInconsistency, getWorkflow) fetch the object from the owner first and then authorize against the owner-reported projectId, so an unreadable object is a 404 and the mutation is never forwarded.
POST /v1/query/cypher without a projectId requires an unrestricted global admin (403 otherwise); with a project named, the scope guard's anchoring applies to every caller including admins.

GET /v1/projects merges the two databases: the project list is read from the knowledge graph, and each project is kept only when Principal.level(project) is non-zero, with the caller's effective role attached, so the SQLite store decides visibility.

Owners.call sends only headers built by the query-service: its own service token as the bearer, plus X-Sandman-Actor user name and X-Sandman-Roles derived from the Principal for user callers; nothing from the user's request is copied, so forged client actor/roles headers never reach an owner, and service/plugin principals are forwarded without an actor.

relay passes owner status and body through unchanged except HTTP 401, which becomes 503 application/problem+json with title "owner rejected the query-service token"; Service.forward converts any httpx.HTTPError (unreachable or unconfigured owner) into 503 "<owner> unavailable".

The transition flow is two-step: the inconsistency detail is fetched from the inconsistency-agent first (owner 404 relayed), a 200 is authorized against its projectId, and only then is the POST forwarded with the body and the project-derived roles header; a non-200 detail is relayed without forwarding.

createIngestion requires multipart/form-data (400 otherwise) and streams the request body to the extraction-agent (request.stream() with forwarded content-type/content-length) rather than buffering it, while checkIngestion relays the JSON manifest.

Forwarded query parameters are filtered to a fixed allowlist: listInconsistencies forwards only status, type, severity, artifactId, changedSince, limit and cursor to the inconsistency-agent; listWorkflows injects projectId and forwards only status, limit, cursor to the orchestrator; createWorkflow injects projectId into the POST body so the caller cannot target another project.

Every console form POST is CSRF-checked: form() returns 403 unless the posted csrf token matches the session's token (or the pre-login sandman_login_csrf cookie for the login form) using a constant-time comparison, and the session and login cookies are HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, path /, Secure only when SANDMAN_COOKIE_SECURE=true.

A user with must_change_password is redirected to /console/password from every console page except /console/password and /console/logout, the password change requires the current password plus at least 12 characters and a different value, and completing it revokes the session; admin-created users and the bootstrap admin always start with the flag set.

The ASGI middleware adds content-security-policy default-src 'self' to responses whose path starts with /console or /static and counts in-flight requests for /v1/status, excluding the QUIET paths /healthz, /readyz and /v1/status from the count.

The console renders projects degradingly: per-project counts, changed-since and workflow-status calls go to the owners, and if an owner is down the page still renders with the workflow column showing "unavailable".

Console "new" badges come from the last_visits table: the inconsistency list reads the previous per-project visit, records a new one, and marks items new when updatedAt is later and the status is OPEN or REOPENED; the projects page asks the owner for changedSince=visit to count the badge.

The console upload page builds the ingestion manifest server-side: archive_manifest streams a zip or tar(.gz), rejecting symlinks, non-regular files, absolute paths, .. segments, duplicate entries and more than 20000 files while computing a sha256 per file, kind_rules parses glob=kind[:format] lines against a fixed kind set, and the result is forwarded as multipart manifest + archive to the extraction-agent.

UserStore is a single SQLite database (SANDMAN_USER_DB, default /data/users.db) with tables users, memberships, tokens, sessions and last_visits, migrations applied from sorted *.sql files in the migrations folder tracked by PRAGMA user_version, and Argon2id password hashes with a pre-computed dummy hash so unknown usernames cost the same work.

Sessions store the sha256 of the session id plus a CSRF token, are valid for 12 hours absolute and 2 hours idle with last_seen touched on each lookup, and disabling a user or changing their password revokes all their sessions; personal tokens store only the sha256 of the secret with optional project scope, maxRole cap and expiry, and find_token records last_used_at on every use and matches only unexpired tokens of enabled users.
The bootstrap admin is created only when the user store is empty, with global role admin and must_change_password set, reading the password from SANDMAN_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE.

The exports read the knowledge graph directly with fixed templates rather than forwarding to an owner: export/tracelinks returns active trace links whose endpoints resolve to current artifact versions with approach, minConfidence and includeRejected filters (CSV default with columns source_key,target_key,link_type,approach,approach_version,confidence,status,run_id), and export/inconsistencies assembles InconsistencyDetail documents with involved entries, evidence, history and the mirrored ADR-0007 allowedTransitions (JSON default, CSV columns id,type,severity,title,status,verification,detector,detectorVersion,confidence,createdAt,updatedAt plus involved and history as JSON cells).

Runner.run is the single guarded read path for user Cypher and the NL stub: it rejects caller params named projectId, cypher or timeout, runs the guard, appends LIMIT limit+1 when the statement has none and always a QUERY MEMORY LIMIT (default 100 MB), caps the timeout at 10 s for users and 30 s for services/plugins, truncates to the requested limit, and post-checks every returned map for project confinement.

POST /v1/query/nl is the M0 regex-intent stub: config/query/intents.yaml maps whole-question patterns to fixed anchored Cypher templates that must pass the guard at load time, an unmatched question returns 422 with the supported intents listed, and mode cypher-only or execute false returns the generated Cypher without running it.

API errors are uniformly application/problem+json: the HTTPException handler renders problems on /v1 paths and the console error template on /console paths (a 303 becomes the redirect), and RequestValidationError becomes a 400 problem with a joined errors list.

GET /v1/status of the query-service allows only unrestricted admins and service callers (plugins and ordinary users get 403) and reports the StatusTracker snapshot whose activeTasks is the middleware's in-flight request count.

The app is built with docs_url, redoc_url and openapi_url disabled because contracts/openapi/query-service.yaml is the authoritative API contract, and the per-operation minimum role (x-sandman-min-role) is loaded from that file at startup and used by authorize.

build() reads SANDMAN_USER_DB, SANDMAN_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE, SANDMAN_COOKIE_SECURE and the three owner URLs (SANDMAN_EXTRACTION_URL, SANDMAN_INCONSISTENCY_URL, SANDMAN_ORCHESTRATOR_URL) directly from the environment; an unset owner maps to http://unconfigured.invalid so its calls fail into 503, and the query-service is published only through the Caddy edge proxy on 127.0.0.1:8080.

Authorization is caller-kind-restricted before the project check: plugins may only run queryCypher and getSchema, service callers may only read (never the USER_ONLY account operations or anything above viewer), admin operations need an unrestricted admin, an unreadable project yields 404 and an insufficient role 403; the authorization test asserts a matrix covering exactly the contract operations across twelve caller kinds.

The ADR-0011 console is server-rendered in the query-service: Jinja2 with autoescape, the vendored htmx 2.0.4 as the only script (configured with allowEval false), no own JavaScript, and it calls the owner REST APIs server-side with the authenticated actor so role checks stay in one place.
